references.text: Abraham complains to Abimelech about the well his servants had seized by force, and they make a covenant. Isaac now reopens the same wells that his father had dug.
The place Beersheba gets its name from the covenant between Abraham and Abimelech concerning the wells—a location central to Isaac's story.
The Philistines had stopped up all the wells that Abraham's servants had dug—this is the direct reason why Isaac had to reopen them.
After reopening Abraham's wells, Isaac's servants also dig new ones, leading to further conflicts with the Philistines.
The context of Isaac's stay in the land of the Philistines and God's promise to give him the land, mirroring the promises given to Abraham.
Both verses illustrate Isaac's strategy for restoring Abraham's inheritance through well-digging and altar-building in the land of the Philistines.
